question: Should the official-publisher admin API expose claimState, officialState, and restrictionState as the durable vocabulary for publisher trust facts once the derivation defect and proof gap are fixed?
rationale: The code can be repaired mechanically, but accepting this vocabulary creates an API and trust-boundary contract that automation should not define without maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept after repair
options.body: Proceed with this API vocabulary after claimed-state derivation requires an observed active user and the contributor posts redacted runtime/API proof.

options.title: Split spec first
options.body: Land only the internal spec now and defer the admin response field until the publisher-state contract is fully decided.

options.title: Choose different vocabulary
options.body: Ask for a revised PR that uses maintainer-selected names or a narrower response shape before clients depend on these fields.

recommendation.title: Accept after repair
recommendation.body: Proceed with this API vocabulary after claimed-state derivation requires an observed active user and the contributor posts redacted runtime/API proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the recent official-publisher admin list and schema history most directly affected by this API contract.
